implementation_notes: Rust's realization is a generic struct plus serde: #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct Envelope<T> { headers: HashMap<String, String>, payload: T } expresses the wrapper with no boilerplate, and serde_json / serde_cbor provide the wire form; on Kafka the transport-side analogue is the record header collection (rdkafka OwnedHeaders, inserted through BaseRecord::headers()). That replaces the classic envelope class - reach for a hand-written codec only when the wire format precedes serde or must stay byte-exact for a non-Rust peer.
pitfalls: serde ignores unknown fields by default and the envelope has no version field unless you add one, which makes forward compatibility accidental rather than designed.
Collecting headers into a HashMap loses duplicates and ordering; broker headers are multi-valued in general, so use a Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> when fidelity matters.
A generic Envelope<T> with a borrowed payload (&str) ties the decoded envelope to the input buffer; owned payloads or explicit lifetimes are required once it outlives the frame.
